newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT-JGBS SEEN STAYING AT HIGHER END OF 126-127.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-JGBS SEEN STAYING AT HIGHER END OF 126-127.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to consolidate at the higher end of 126.00-127.00 on Friday, ahead of the release of key economic data later in the day.

Japan will release machinery orders data for June and a forecast for the July to September quarter at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT). Weak machinery orders data may lift the September contract above its recent high of 126.91. But otherwise, profit-taking from those who had built longs earlier this week may cap the topside at 126.60-126.80, traders said.
On Thursday, the September ended Tokyo at 126.50.

"It seems difficult for the contract to rise above 126.91 today after falls in U.S. Treasuries overnight and due to pre-weekend position adjustments," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "But if the machinery data is weak, in contrast to what many now expect, that may enable the September to break through above that level," he said.

A Reuter poll shows economists forecast the machinery orders to fall by 1.5 to 13 percent in June from a month earlier. But some economists recently revised their forecasts upward due to improvement in certain areas of private orders, traders said.
